name: Anthracene Purple
lede: Anthracene Purple is a dark, muted brownish purple from Ridgway's 1912 chart, one of a dozen names the ISCC-NBS system groups under a single color block.

sections.title: A block of a dozen names
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 plate XLIV gives this color the name Anthracene Purple, hue 69′′′, tone k, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it in block 229 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[log-cabin]], [[vivid-taupe-brown]], [[dark-naphthalene-violet]] and [[starling]], at 3.7, 4.4, 4.4 and 5.4 ΔE [1]. The same ISCC-NBS block groups at least eleven other names as near-duplicates, among them Turtledove, Blue Fox and Mauve Dust [1]. Among named purples and browns it sits near [[mauve]] and [[taupe]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 225 of 23,781 paintings, 0.95 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is Ambrogio Lorenzetti's St. John the Baptist, from 1337, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It peaks in the 1910s, in 14 of 523 paintings, at 4.9 times the archive's overall rate, and Gustave Caillebotte carries it in four of his 22 paintings here, well above his own museums' baseline [2]. Inside a painting it splits between shadow and mid-tone, 50 and 46 percent of its appearances [2].
